verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.26
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 9.26

verses.pali: 3. Sattāvāsavagga
verses.english: 3. Abodes of Sentient Beings

verses.pali: Silāyūpasutta
verses.english: The Simile of the Stone Post
So I have heard.

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca candikāputto rājagahe viharanti veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

verses.pali: Tatra kho āyasmā candikāputto bhikkhū āmantesi (…):
verses.english: There Venerable Candikāputta addressed the mendicants,

verses.pali: “devadatto, āvuso, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
verses.english: “Reverends, Devadatta teaches the mendicants like this:

verses.pali: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
verses.english: ‘When a mendicant’s mind is solidified by heart, it’s appropriate for them to say:

verses.pali: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
verses.english: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ candikāputtaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to him,

verses.pali: “na kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
verses.english: “Reverend Candikāputta, Devadatta does not teach the mendicants like that.

verses.pali: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
Evañca kho, āvuso, candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
verses.english: He teaches like this:

verses.pali: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
verses.english: ‘When a mendicant’s mind is well consolidated by heart, it’s appropriate for them to say:

verses.pali: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
verses.english: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’”

verses.pali: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā candikāputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: For a second time …

verses.pali: “devadatto, āvuso, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
Dutiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ candikāputtaṁ etadavoca:
“na kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
Evañca kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā candikāputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: And for a third time Venerable Candikāputta addressed the mendicants …

verses.pali: “devadatto, āvuso, bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’”ti.
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ candikāputtaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: And for a third time, Sāriputta said to him,

verses.pali: “na kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
verses.english: “Reverend Candikāputta, Devadatta does not teach the mendicants like that.

verses.pali: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā citaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
Evañca kho, āvuso candikāputta, devadatto bhikkhūnaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
verses.english: He teaches like this:

verses.pali: ‘yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti, tassetaṁ bhikkhuno kallaṁ veyyākaraṇāya—
verses.english: ‘When a mendicant’s mind is well consolidated by heart, it’s appropriate for them to say:

verses.pali: khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.
verses.english: “I understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”’

verses.pali: Kathañca, āvuso, bhikkhuno cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti?
verses.english: And how is a mendicant’s mind well consolidated by heart?

verses.pali: ‘Vītarāgaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: The mind is well consolidated by heart when they know: ‘My mind is without greed.’

verses.pali: ‘vītadosaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: … ‘My mind is without hate.’

verses.pali: ‘vītamohaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: … ‘My mind is without delusion.’

verses.pali: ‘asarāgadhammaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: … ‘My mind is not liable to become greedy.’

verses.pali: ‘asadosadhammaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: … ‘My mind is not liable to become hateful.’

verses.pali: ‘asamohadhammaṁ me cittan’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: … ‘My mind is not liable to become deluded.’

verses.pali: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ kāmabhavāyā’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the sensual realm.’

verses.pali: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ rūpabhavāyā’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti;
verses.english: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the realm of luminous form.’

verses.pali: ‘anāvattidhammaṁ me cittaṁ arūpabhavāyā’ti cetasā cittaṁ suparicitaṁ hoti.
verses.english: … ‘My mind is not liable to return to rebirth in the formless realm.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ sammā vimuttacittassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti;
verses.english: When a mendicant’s mind is rightly freed like this, even if compelling sights come into the range of vision they don’t occupy their mind.

verses.pali: amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ, vayaṁ cassānupassati.
verses.english: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, silāyūpo soḷasakukkuko.
verses.english: Suppose there was a stone post, sixteen feet long.

verses.pali: Tassassu aṭṭha kukkū heṭṭhā nemaṅgamā, aṭṭha kukkū upari nemassa.
verses.english: Eight feet were buried underground, and eight above ground.

verses.pali: Atha puratthimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva naṁ saṅkampeyya na sampavedheyya;
verses.english: And violent storms were to blow up out of the east, the west, the north, and the south.

verses.pali: atha pacchimāya …
atha uttarāya …
atha dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva naṁ saṅkampeyya na sampavedheyya.
verses.english: They couldn’t make it tremor and tremble and quake.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Gambhīrattā, āvuso, nemassa, sunikhātattā silāyūpassa.
verses.english: It’s because that stone post is firmly embedded, with deep foundations.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, sammā vimuttacittassa bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti;
verses.english: In the same way, when a mendicant’s mind is rightly freed like this, even if compelling sights come into the range of vision they don’t occupy their mind.

verses.pali: amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ, vayaṁ cassānupassati.
verses.english: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.

verses.pali: Bhusā cepi sotaviññeyyā saddā …
verses.english: If even compelling sounds …

verses.pali: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …
verses.english: smells …

verses.pali: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …
verses.english: tastes …

verses.pali: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā …
verses.english: touches …

verses.pali: manoviññeyyā dhammā manassa āpāthaṁ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṁ pariyādiyanti;
verses.english: and ideas come into the range of the mind they don’t occupy the mind.

verses.pali: amissīkatamevassa cittaṁ hoti ṭhitaṁ āneñjappattaṁ, vayaṁ cassānupassatī”ti.
verses.english: Their mind is quite untainted. It is steady, imperturbable, observing disappearance.”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
